author: John Pierson
title: 'A dream come true': East Haven's Constantinople goes pro with PWHL - NewsBreak
text:
By John Pierson Jason Levy ,
1 days ago
EAST HAVEN, Conn. (WTNH) — East Haven’s Jules Constantinople is now a pro on the ice as her dream came true last week after a decorated college hockey career at Northeastern.
Hartford Yard Goats are playoff-bound for 2nd time in 3 seasons Constantinople was drafted by the Vancouver Goldeneyes with the 25th overall pick in the Professional Women’s Hockey League (PWHL) Draft.
A two-way defensive star for the Huskies, the 5-foot-5 blueliner was the Hockey East Best Defender this past season. She had 24 points as a senior and 63 for her career. She likes to mix it up and block shots.
Constantinople is still processing it all before she heads to Vancouver in November for the start of the PWHL season.
“I was really anxious, and then when you hear your name get called, you kind of black out,” Constantinople said. “But it was a dream come true. So many emotions. (It) still hasn’t hit me yet.”
Constantinople said it took a lot of hard work and dedication and thanked her family for making sacrifices to help her get this far.
“I don’t regret anything. I love stepping on the ice every day,” she said. “If you don’t love it, what is the point at the end of the day?”
